related_work: Ryan used some famous thinkers. Roland Barthes said “line is action become visible”. Eisenstein said we know Disney characters are drawings, but we feel them as alive. McLuhan said media changes us, so maybe we are the ones being “animated”. Heidegger said technology is really about what it does to our thinking.
conclusion_future_work: I learned that animation is not just moving pictures. It also changes how we see and feel. This week, I need to make a short animation.
results_discussion: We watched films like A Trip to the Moon, Fantasmagorie, Ballet mécanique and Duck Amuck. Early animation was very free and wild, and everything could change shape, like a tree that laughs. When sound came, animation grew fast, because sound could be made later and added to the picture. The last film, by Don Hertzfeldt, used only stick figures, but it was very emotional. This shows that even a simple line can have strong feeling.
title: week6
introduction: This week, Ryan talked about the history of animation, from 1900 to the 2010s. His main idea was that animation moves, but it is not alive. We know it’s just drawings, but we still feel it is alive. He also showed us many short films.
